top_moves.title: Mistral previews Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter model with open weights due end of October
top_moves.body: Mistral launched a **Large 4 preview**: a mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters, API-priced at $1.36/M input and $4.18/M output, with weights promised by month-end. For clients with EU data-residency or self-hosting requirements this is the first frontier-scale option that could run inside their own recovery boundary.

top_moves.title: Anthropic folds Project Glasswing into a three-tier Cyber Verification Program; partners verified 129,000+ flaws
top_moves.body: Glasswing partners confirmed **129,000+ software flaws between April and July, 33,000+ rated critical or high**. That volume is the planning number: patch windows and vulnerability-driven outage scenarios in BIAs need to assume AI-speed discovery on both sides.

top_moves.title: Google cuts Gemini model access for free and AI Plus personal accounts on Oct 9
top_moves.body: From Oct 9, free personal accounts drop to **Flash-Lite only**; AI Plus keeps Flash but loses Gemini Pro on dates sent by email. Pro and Ultra are unchanged, and the notice does not cover Workspace accounts — but anyone doing client work on a personal Gemini login will see quality drop this week.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Publishes 722 math manuscripts from an unreleased internal model and opens a Decisions API beta on GPT-6 Luna.
providers.detail: On Oct 6 OpenAI pushed 722 mathematics manuscripts (372 families of results, Apache-2.0) to GitHub, crediting an unnamed internal frontier model and saying nearly all came from a single prompt to one agent. The same day a Decisions API entered public beta on GPT-6 Luna at $0.10 per million input tokens, pitched as up to 10x faster than the Responses API for classification-style calls. No change to ChatGPT plans or data terms today.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Cyber Verification Program replaces Project Glasswing with three tiers; IPO still expected despite market jitters.
providers.detail: The Oct 6 announcement consolidates Glasswing into a three-tier Cyber Verification Program and reports 129,000+ verified flaws found by partners between April and July, 33,000+ of them critical or high. Anthropic also expanded its Claude Startups program during SF Tech Week ($1,000 API credit, a free year of Claude Team for up to five Premium seats). CNN reported Oct 5 that the IPO remains on track despite AI-slowdown calls. No new model today; Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain current.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Personal-account model tiers tighten Oct 9; Nano Banana 2.1 halves image pricing; 3,590 MW Constellation power deal.
providers.detail: From Oct 9 free personal accounts get Flash-Lite only and AI Plus loses Gemini Pro (dates by email); AI Pro and Ultra keep all three models and Deep Think. Workspace and school accounts are not covered by the notice. Google also released Nano Banana 2.1 (up to 14 reference images, roughly 50% cheaper per image) and signed a 20-year, 3,590 MW power agreement with Constellation, about a quarter of it from new nuclear capacity.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Quiet — no new release found; Grok 5 by Oct 31 remains a prediction-market question, not an announcement.
providers.detail: Today's searches surfaced no new xAI release or policy change. Prediction markets are still pricing a Grok 5 launch before year-end, but xAI has announced no date.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: Meta and Sierra publish the Personal Agent Protocol, an OAuth-based standard for AI agents to authenticate with businesses.
providers.detail: Announced Oct 6 with founding partners Walmart, Shopify, Stripe, Rocket, Genesys and Instinct. It defines how a consumer's AI agent proves identity and authority to a business system. Worth tracking for any client with customer-facing portals: agent logins are a new access path that identity, fraud and continuity plans do not yet cover. No Llama release today.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: Large 4 preview: 1-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, $1.36/$4.18 per million tokens, weights by end of October.
providers.detail: Large 4 has 49B active parameters and was trained over two months on 4,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs. It is available now in preview through the API, with open weights promised by month-end. This breaks a week-long quiet streak and is Mistral's most significant model release of the year.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: Quiet — no new feature or policy change found today.
providers.detail: Searches returned only older material (Computer by email, finance data sources, Model Council). Nothing dated in the last 48 hours.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Copilot Search gains in-results chat; SharePoint Copilot can split, reorder and extract PDF sections.
providers.detail: The Oct 6 release notes add conversational follow-up directly inside Copilot Search results. Copilot in SharePoint's October update works on PDFs at page and section level — extract sections, reorder pages, split a document. The redesigned Copilot in Edge (new icon, Voice and Vision) begins rolling out mid-October with no admin action; the Word entry-point change reaches GCC, GCC High and DoD tenants this month.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: Minor: IDE update required to restore agent activity in usage metrics; model deprecations from Oct 2 still in force.
providers.detail: The only new changelog entry (Oct 6) asks admins to update IDEs so agent activity reappears in Copilot usage metrics. Earlier this month: computer use for desktop apps (Oct 1), code review API and new default effort level (Oct 2), and a batch of model deprecations (Oct 2).

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new ship found today.
providers.detail: Nothing dated in the last 48 hours surfaced in today's research.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: Still quiet — no update found since the June Gamma Agent/3.0 launch.
providers.detail: No dated release or pricing change surfaced. Search results were evergreen comparison pieces only.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new ship found today.
providers.detail: Nothing dated in the last 48 hours surfaced; Notion 3.7 skills (Sept 15) remains the latest release on record.

month_themes.then: Undisclosed agent activity on public sites (OpenAI); a 100-company warning on AI-enabled cyberattacks; AI agents gaining a standard interface to lab hardware (Anthropic).
month_themes.now: Frontier-scale open weights from Europe (Mistral Large 4); AI vulnerability discovery quantified at 129,000+ flaws; consumer tiers tightening while enterprise tiers hold (Gemini).

habits.shift: No change. Add a vulnerability-surge scenario to runbooks: the Glasswing figures (33,000+ critical/high flaws in four months) justify an emergency-patching playbook alongside the ransomware one.
NIST's draft SP 1353 (generative AI for CSF 2.0 work) closes for comment Oct 15 — read it now so client guidance cites the draft rather than vendor blogs.
Add Mistral Large 4 to the shortlist for clients needing EU-hosted or self-hosted models; hold any recommendation until weights and licence terms land at month-end.
No change. If you or a client drafts on a personal Gemini account, expect weaker output after Oct 9 unless the account is AI Pro or Ultra.
No change. Gamma remains quiet; keep it as a formatting fallback only.
No change. NotebookLM on a Workspace account is unaffected by the Oct 9 personal-tier cut.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.shift: Two talking points this week: executives from four labs declined under oath to guarantee agents always follow safeguards, and the Meta/Sierra Personal Agent Protocol means customer AI agents will start logging in to business systems.

community.signal: Mistral Large 4's promised open weights are the natural focus for the local-model crowd; the long-running thread arguing that the June Fable 5 / Mythos 5 suspension proves the case for local models keeps resurfacing.
community.so_what: Self-hosting as a continuity control is now a mainstream argument — expect clients to raise it.

community.signal: No standout post verifiable this week; the standing usage-limits and performance megathreads remain the centre of gravity.
community.so_what: Rate limits are still the main practical risk for Claude-dependent workflows — keep a second tool ready.

community.signal: No high-engagement thread could be verified from today's searches.
community.so_what: Treat as no signal rather than good news.

watch.title: Oct 9 — Gemini personal-tier model cut
watch.body: Free accounts drop to Flash-Lite; AI Plus loses Gemini Pro on emailed dates. Check which account type any client-facing work actually runs on.

watch.title: Oct 15 — NIST SP 1353 comment deadline
watch.body: Draft quick-start guide on using generative AI for Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 analysis, planning and reporting. Final version will shape how auditors view AI-assisted compliance work.

watch.title: Oct 19 — GitHub Copilot model cut-off
watch.body: Deprecated models stop working. Teams with pinned models in automation should confirm replacements before then.

watch.title: End of October — Mistral Large 4 weights
watch.body: Licence terms and hardware requirements decide whether this is genuinely self-hostable for regulated clients or a headline only.

watch.title: Agent authentication standards
watch.body: Personal Agent Protocol (Meta/Sierra, with Walmart, Shopify and Stripe) is the first broad attempt at agent login. Watch for fraud-control and audit-log guidance before clients enable it.
